headline: The jury in Qualcomm's contract lawsuit against Arm will return next week after deliberating on Friday, so there is still no verdict.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a closely watched chip-licensing case with a verdict now delayed, but nothing is decided yet.
importance_line: A verdict could change how much Qualcomm pays Arm for the chip designs behind its processors, which matters to the two companies and the phone makers that use Qualcomm chips, but there is no verdict yet, Arm denies the claims, and the judge has not ruled on Qualcomm's bid to stop paying royalties for five years.
summary: Reuters reports that the jury in Qualcomm's lawsuit against Arm Holdings, which supplies chip-design technology to Qualcomm and others, will return next week after deliberations on Friday 9 Oct 2026 in Wilmington, Delaware, so a verdict is still pending. It must decide whether Arm broke its licensing agreements by holding back software patches and tools and whether it tried to sabotage Qualcomm's dealings with Meta Platforms by leaking a 2024 letter; we carried the opening of the trial in our 6 Oct 2026 edition.
notes: The Reuters article itself is blocked (HTTP 401). The 'jury returns next week' detail comes only from Reuters' headline; the trial background is from Reuters' earlier same-day preview (read on Yahoo Finance, 9 Oct) and from Tech Times (jury began deliberating Friday morning, no verdict at publication). Trial opened Mon 5 Oct and ran five days; our 6 Oct edition carried the opening (item 52). The $1.5 billion royalty figure in Tech Times is an analyst estimate and was not used.
